issues.description: Attribute type mismatch for 'lectureName': the problem statement and UML describe lectureName as a String, and the template expects a simple attribute to be added, but the solution introduces a custom LectureName class and makes the lectureName field of type LectureName. This structural difference will confuse students about the expected type and API for getters/setters and deviates from the UML/specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the UML/problem statement by using a String for the lectureName attribute (change the field and constructor parameter to String, remove or avoid using a LectureName wrapper). Alternatively, if the LectureName type is intended pedagogically, update the problem statement and template to mention and include the LectureName class so students know to use it.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: the problem statement requires a constructor that initializes lectureName as a String (and other primitive attributes in the specified order), but the solution's constructor expects a LectureName object for the lectureName parameter. This prevents students from following the constructor signature implied by the UML and template.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution constructor signature to accept a String lectureName (and keep the parameter order matching the UML). If the LectureName wrapper is intentional, update the problem statement and template to specify the LectureName type and provide the LectureName class in the template.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the lectureName attribute as a String (lectureName: String) and expect the constructor to initialize it in that form. The solution implementation, however, introduces a new type LectureName and defines the lectureName attribute and constructor parameter as LectureName. This changes the conceptual representation of the same entity (the lecture's name) across artifacts and will confuse students: they will expect to use plain Strings when implementing and testing the template but the solution uses a custom LectureName class.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the lecture name across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to use a plain String for lectureName (replace the LectureName class with a String-typed lectureName field, update the constructor and getters/setters accordingly), or (B) update the problem statement and UML to explicitly document the LectureName value object and require students to use it. Option A is recommended for minimal cognitive overhead for students.
